baseline.rule: Preserve every preexisting change; never reset, discard, overwrite, or mix unrelated work into the multiproduct delivery.

phase1B.goal: Represent products, plans, optional modules, subscriptions, and effective entitlements without changing the existing Agenda behavior.
requiredRules: Every plan belongs to exactly one product.
Every subscription belongs to exactly one product and its plan must belong to the same product.
A billing customer may have at most one non-cancelled subscription per product.
Modules are optional capabilities owned by one product.
A subscribed module must belong to the same product as the subscription.
Entitlements are evaluated on the server and default to denied when absent.
Agenda access remains equivalent to the behavior before this migration.
The legacy saas_clients.plan field remains compatible and is not repurposed as the source of multiproduct truth.
The existing billing synchronization trigger must affect only the Agenda subscription until checkout becomes multiproduct-aware.
No planned product is exposed to a business without an explicit active or trial subscription.
All exposed tables use explicit grants and RLS.
Privileged helpers live in the private schema, revoke PUBLIC execution, validate auth.uid(), and expose only narrow wrappers when required.
acceptance: A migrated Agenda customer retains access and limits without manual action.
A business without a Cardápio subscription cannot use protected Cardápio administration.
A business may hold Agenda and Cardápio subscriptions simultaneously.
Cancelling one product does not cancel or suspend another product.
A module cannot be attached across products or tenants.
Cross-tenant reads and writes fail in database tests.
All database tests pass on a fresh local replay.
Supabase database advisors report no unresolved security findings introduced by the migration.
No remote environment is changed without a separate authorization.
